title.narrative: Support to Stop Tuberculosis Partnership from USAID

description.narrative:
Support to Stop Tuberculosis Partnership through three areas:
1) Cross –cutting support for Global Fund TB grant implementation (through Human resources support for health, procurement supply chain and data systems: USAID TB supports up to three long-term advisors to work With Stop TB and the Global Fund ta strengthen Global Fund TB grant implementation and improve coordination among TB partners. These technical experts will work closely With the Global Fund TB Technical Advisors to provide overall TB technical support to the Global Fund TB Secretariat. They Will also assist with policy development and planning related to their areas of expertise, human resource management, and supply chain improvement. 

2) Support to the Scaling Up Nutrition (SUN) movement Secretariat
Support for improved accountability by all SUN stakeholders to achieve the goals outlined in the SUN Movement Strategy and Roadmap and to SUN countries to strengthen in-country capacity to design, implement and monitor multi-sectoral nutrition programs coordinated by stakeholders 

3) MDR-TB Technical Assistance Support for Afghanistan
The purpose of the MDR-TB (multidrug-resistant tuberculosis) consultant is to provide technical support, both clinical and programmatic, for the introduction of new medicines and novel regimens in Afghanistan. The consultant will support the National Tuberculosis Control Programme to develop a comprehensive plan on how to rapidly scale up shortened regimen and new drugs.

UNOPS hosts the Stop Tuberculosis Partnership Secretariat (STBP) as of 1 January 2015, in Geneva, Switzerland. The vision of the Stop TB Partnership is to realize the goal of elimination of Tuberculosis (TB) as a public health problem and, ultimately, to obtain a world free of TB by ensuring that every TB patient has access to effective diagnosis, treatment and cure; stopping transmission of TB; reducing the inequitable social and economic toll of TB; and developing and implementing new preventive, diagnostic and therapeutic tools and strategies. The Stop Partnership is uniquely positioned to support the development and further implementation by partners of the current and future Global Plan, acting as a coordinator and catalyst for the range of partners engaged in the fight against TB.
